headline: El Niño weather phenomenon drives food price inflation in Peru
summary: Wholesale prices for corn have risen over 100% since January due to the El Niño phenomenon. Further price increases for tubers and poultry are expected as weather conditions continue to pressure food markets in Lima.
why: Food price volatility is a major component of headline inflation in emerging markets, directly impacting consumer purchasing power and central bank policy.

impacts.name: Corn
impacts.why: Supply disruptions caused by El Niño are directly driving up wholesale food costs.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Supply chain disruptions caused by extreme weather directly reduce the availability of agricultural goods, leading to higher market prices.
